# Execution loop — claim to close

The tree is a record, not a deliverable. A tree write rides the code commit that earned it: a
status flip, an owner, a `done:` line or a `changelog:` line goes in the same pathspec as the work.
A feature costs at most two tree-only commits, one that opens it and one that closes it. Never a
commit per flip. Run `make check` before the commit, so a record's format fault is fixed in it
rather than in a follow-up.

**Before you plan or stop, invoke the skill installed beside this rule:** `writing-plans` (plan
only when needed) or `executing-plans` (file and continue). Told "use the sdlc, get to work"?
`run-the-sdlc` is the orchestrator's loop, with its commands.

## The rungs — never run one wider than what you changed

    may I start?            pm ready-for story <id>     the entry edge; runs nothing
    a PM-tree or doc edit   make check                  the static gates alone
    an edit, inner loop     verify --story              what [verify] story names
    before a commit         make precommit              check + your narrow tier
    closing a story         close story <id> [<id> …]   its checks, then `done`
    closing a feature       close feature <id> [<id> …] runs what [verify] feature names
    closing a milestone     release <version>           its `gate` check is the full gate

`make sdlc ARGS='verify --plan'` prints each rung with the cost it last took, from your ledger.
Ask it rather than guess.

**Every rung has an entry edge: `make pm ARGS='ready-for story|feature|milestone|tag <id>'`.**
Exit 0 ready, 1 not ready naming every blocker, 2 usage. It writes, runs and boots nothing, so
ask it instead of guessing whether the work below you is finished:

    ready-for story <id>       the story belt's checks decidable BEFORE the work, and
                               every check it did not ask, named with why
    ready-for feature <id>     every story in the `done` category?
    ready-for milestone <id>   every feature done with a review record, no open bug?
                               under `reconcile: forward`, a complete record?
    ready-for tag <id>         every finding at a disposition other than `open`?

There is no `ready-for adopt`: `make sdlc ARGS='adopt <version>'` is checks only and writes
nothing. Where `[emit]` declares a sink, each rung files a `rung.enter` event.

**A belt is its checks, then one write or a clean error** (D12). `close story`, `close feature`,
`release` and `adopt` print one line per check, then write the grain's status (the first state of
its kind's `done` list) or write nothing, name every false check and exit 1. `--force` writes
anyway, and the ledger's `deviation` row names the false checks. Nothing is pushed or tagged; what
is yours next is printed as `next:` lines. **Close one by one, the moment a close is ready**: a
feature closes when its review record lands, in one command, `close feature <id> --review-record
<path>`, which stamps `reviewed:` only if the belt writes `done`. A lane with no reviewer closes
the moment it merges and its record is written. The many-id form, `close story <id> <id> …` or
`close feature <id> <id> …`, is for grains that became ready TOGETHER; it runs the rung (and
`committed`) once and writes each grain on its own verdict. It is never a reason to wait. `make
check` ends its verdict line with `; N close(s) ready to run — <command>` while one stands open, and the
stock stop gate holds the session's stop on it. A rung whose inputs have not moved since its last PASS
is reused, not re-run: every rung's state leaves out what a belt writes (a `status:` line, the
belt's ledger rows), so one close does not re-buy the next, and `release` reuses a green
`verify --milestone`. A project whose rung target READS statuses sets `[verify]
reuse_ignores_status = false`. A verified change whose status never moved is the tree and the
work disagreeing, so the close follows the merge, not the end of the day.

## States, and moving them

The states are this project's `[pm.states.<kind>]` in `devkit.toml`; `pm vocabulary` prints them
and is the authority. Every question the tool asks is asked of a state's CATEGORY (`todo`,
`in_progress`, `done`), never of the word, and nothing enforces which state follows which. A
`done`-category state means everything inside the tree's authority is finished, or abandoned for
`obe`. Shipping is a git event after it.

Each kind moves with its own verb, `pm story|feature|bug|milestone <state> <id>`, to a state that
kind declares; any other is refused at exit 2 naming `[pm.states.<kind>]`.

1. **Claim.** `pm story building <id>` and `pm set <id> owner <name>`. This is bookkeeping only: a
   ledger row files against its grain's milestone at any status, so the flip does not turn
   recording on.
2. **Commit atomically**, one logical unit per commit, the tree writes it earned in its pathspec.
3. **Review is a FEATURE act.** A feature moves to `reviewing` where the vocabulary declares it,
   while its review record is written. The stock story vocabulary has no review word; a finished
   story goes to `done` through `close story`.
4. **Close the feature** with `close feature <id> --review-record <path>` when its record lands
   (`close feature <id>` when `reviewed:` is already stamped), or by hand with
   `pm feature done <id> --review-record <path>`, which sets the status and touches nothing else. A
   `done` parent over a child not in `done` FAILS `check pm` D11. Close each story by name.
5. **Move `status:` with the CLI, never an editor.** It rewrites one line and preserves every other
   byte, line endings included. `pm new milestone|feature|story|bug` creates a grain at its
   initial status, id `<kind-prefix>-<slug>` (`ms-`, `ft-`, `st-`, `bg-`). The parent argument is
   the binding it writes, never part of the id, so re-parenting is one `pm set`. A bug may be
   created without a name (a `next:` line names its empty `name:`). A milestone or feature id
   already in the tree, with the name omitted, fills its missing slots.
6. **Leave evidence at close** (below).

Who flips a feature to review and closes it is your project's call; the tool permits either.

## What the CLI refuses, and what it reports

It refuses facts about the INPUT and reports everything else:

- **A status you ASK for that the kind does not declare** is an error naming
  `[pm.states.<kind>]`. An undeclared status already in the file is what it says now, and the move
  repairs it (`wombat -> building`); `check pm` D4 reports that drift.
- **`--review-record <path>` naming no file** is refused whole: no stamp, no story touched.
- **Malformed frontmatter** is refused, because there is nowhere to put the field.
- **A feature or milestone move is never refused over its children.** What the tree is then left
  holding is `check pm`'s D5/D11 question.

Every command is idempotent. Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` refused, `2` usage or config error.

## Close evidence

**Bar: a fresh session with no context picks up from the tree alone.**

| close | write | where | budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| story | `done: <hash(es)> — <what shipped>` + any finding line | the story file | ≤5 lines |
| feature | the review record + findings the NEXT feature needs | `[pm] review_dir` | scale to the feature |
| milestone | pointers | the milestone file | a line + a link |

**Never write what is derivable.** `pm status` gives status and tallies, `git log` gives history.
Do not hand-maintain a story list in a feature file or a feature list in a milestone file: that is
a second scoreboard, and it will lie. Sequence is `order:` on the parent, written by `pm add`.

## Habits measured on real milestones

- **A milestone in a `todo`-category state is frozen.** Dispatch nothing and move no status under
  it until the milestone itself moves to an `in_progress`-category state.
- **Ask "who needs it?" before a note becomes a grain.** If no reader and no gate needs it, it
  stays a note.
- **A decision lives at one grain.** Other grains point at it and do not restate it.
- **A review is sized to its feature.** A small feature gets a short record.
- **The tree is shared.** History moves forward only: do not amend, rebase or reset a commit that
  another session can see. Never a broad `pkill`: stop only the process you started. Re-derive
  line numbers before each edit, because another session can move them.
- **A grain's `changelog:` line is the hook plus the why**, in one sentence a consumer reads. Read
  the source before you write it, not only the brief. Work that no consumer can see gets `none`.

## Keeping the tree honest: ask, never hand-copy

- `pm status [<milestone>]` — the whole tree, each parent's children in its `order:`.
- `pm add <parent-id> <child-id> [--position N | --before <id> | --after <id>]` binds and
  sequences in one act; `pm remove` is the pair. An unsequenced child is counted, never a finding.
- `pm list [--status …] [--category …] [--owner …] [--milestone …]` — one tab-separated row per
  story. `pm list --category in_progress` is what is open right now.
- `pm validate` — well-formed frontmatter, bindings to grains of the right kind, resolving
  `depends_on`/`consumed_by`, an acyclic graph. A ref into a retired milestone is UNVERIFIABLE, not
  a failure. `check pm` is the same rules plus status drift, as a gate.
- `pm vocabulary [--json]` — the categories, each kind's states, and the rule ids `[pm] checks` may
  name. Read it after a devkit pin bump.
- **`make sdlc ARGS='dispatch --grain <id>'`** — the prompt a subagent gets, RENDERED from
  `devkit.toml` so it cannot go stale: the grain, the ladder, the gates, the vocabulary. A
  dispatched agent receives none of the files you are reading now, so run it before writing a
  dispatch. Its `GDK-STAMP` line attributes the dispatch's ledger rows to the grain. The
  SubagentStop courier files the dispatch's row — tokens, tool calls, duration — when the agent
  returns; nothing is recorded by hand. `pm ledger record` remains for a dispatch no courier saw.
- **`GDK_LEDGER_GRAIN`** attributes a SESSION: export it, and the couriers file the session's rows
  on that grain. No hook payload carries a grain, and nothing exports it for you. Unset is normal:
  a row then names the one story in progress, or no grain when there are none or several. It never
  guesses.
- `pm ledger show <grain-id>` — that grain's TELEMETRY, oldest first: every status flip, decision
  and dispatch, with the seconds between them. What a story cost, not where it is.
- `pm ledger report [<grain-id>]` — the milestone's units of work (`unit grain issue agent start
  stop duration tokens outcome`), spend `by agent` with each agent's `share`, and `time per state`
  rolled up grain by grain. `open_s` is a clock still running and is never folded into a closed
  total. A feature or story id reports that subtree. `--tree` prints the rows no milestone owns,
  with what the gates cost. **Every telemetry question is comparative, so name more than one
  milestone:** `pm ledger report <a> <b>` gives each block one row per milestone and a `delta` row.
  `--help` names every block's columns in order; the shell is the filter, never a new flag. Do not
  hand-write a table of any of this.
